description: We are EUREKA GIRLS, five ambitious young women from Panama passionate about science, technology, and innovation. We believe great ideas can change the world. Using teamwork, creativity, and NASA’s data, we aim to create meaningful solutions to real-world problems and challenge ourselves!
summary:
TERRA VISION – Know Your Land, Cultivate Your Future 🌱🛰️

TERRA VISION is an innovative web platform developed to help farmers and livestock producers make better agricultural decisions by combining NASA satellite data, climate information, and local farming knowledge.

Our project addresses the challenges of drought, excessive rainfall, soil degradation, and unpredictable weather conditions, particularly in Los Santos, Panama, a region vulnerable to water scarcity.

Using Google AI Studio, we developed an interactive platform designed to help users explore their farms, visualize environmental indicators, identify potential risks, and receive data-informed crop recommendations.

The prototype focuses on five real farming locations: Los Olivos, El Bongo, Tonosí, La Yeguada, and Macaracas. By incorporating interviews with local producers, TERRA VISION connects scientific information with real agricultural needs.

Our goal is to make satellite technology accessible and understandable to farmers, helping them manage water resources, plan planting seasons, protect their land, and improve agricultural sustainability.

TERRA VISION transforms complex environmental information into practical knowledge for a more resilient agricultural future.
details:
TERRA VISION – Project Details

What does our project do, and how does it work?

TERRA VISION is an interactive web platform designed to help farmers and livestock producers understand their land and make better agricultural decisions using NASA Earth observation data, climate information, and local agricultural knowledge.

The platform allows users to select a farm, explore its characteristics, review available environmental indicators such as temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, and vegetation health (NDVI), and identify potential environmental risks.

It also includes a crop evaluation feature designed to compare farm conditions with the requirements of different crops, providing understandable recommendations and highlighting missing information.

Our prototype focuses on five farming locations in Panama: Los Olivos, El Bongo, Tonosí, La Yeguada, and Macaracas. These locations represent different agricultural activities, including livestock production and the cultivation of corn, rice, watermelon, pigeon peas, and forage grass.

What benefits does TERRA VISION offer?

TERRA VISION aims to make environmental information more accessible to farmers who may not have specialized technical knowledge.

Its main benefits include:

  • Better agricultural planning: Helping producers consider weather conditions and crop requirements before planting.
  • Improved water management: Identifying potential water shortages and periods of excessive rainfall.
  • Environmental awareness: Supporting the monitoring of vegetation and environmental conditions.
  • Informed crop selection: Comparing available farm information with agricultural requirements.
  • Accessible technology: Presenting complex information through a simple, visual, Spanish-language interface.

What is the intended impact?

Our project was inspired by real challenges identified through interviews with farmers in Los Santos, Panama.

For example, at Los Olivos, three of the property’s four wells commonly dry up during the dry season, while areas near the La Villa River may experience flooding during heavy rainfall. In Macaracas, a corn producer explained how dependence on rainfall can affect seed germination and crop development.

These experiences demonstrate the importance of providing farmers with accessible environmental information.

Our long-term goal is to help agricultural communities reduce climate-related risks, manage natural resources more efficiently, and improve their resilience to changing environmental conditions.

What tools and technologies did we use?

We developed the web application prototype using Google AI Studio, an AI-assisted development environment that helps generate and refine application components through natural-language instructions.

Our project also draws on research involving NASA Earth observation technologies, including:

  • NASA POWER: Climate information such as temperature and precipitation.
  • NASA GPM: Satellite-based precipitation estimates.
  • NASA SMAP: Soil moisture observations.
  • NASA Earthdata: Access to Earth observation datasets.

We also conducted interviews with local agricultural producers and reviewed agricultural information relevant to Panama.

The prototype was designed to support these data sources, although not all satellite integrations or farm-specific measurements have been fully implemented and validated.

What makes our project creative?

TERRA VISION combines space technology with the real experiences of local farmers.

Rather than developing a platform based only on satellite information, we incorporated the knowledge of producers who understand their land through years of experience.

Our approach makes scientific information more practical by connecting environmental indicators with real agricultural decisions.

Another important feature is our focus on accessibility. We want farmers to understand the information without needing expertise in satellite technology, programming, or environmental science.

What factors did our team consider?

During development, we considered the specific challenges faced by agricultural communities in Panama, including water scarcity, seasonal rainfall, flooding, soil conditions, crop requirements, and access to technology.

We also prioritized ease of use, reliable information, low-cost development, and the distinction between verified measurements, regional estimates, and observations reported by farmers.

Our vision is to make TERRA VISION a bridge between NASA’s Earth observation technology and the everyday decisions of farmers, contributing to a more informed, sustainable, and climate-resilient agricultural future.
